body_md:
\label{the:main}
    Let $u^0 \in C^2({\mathbb{R}}^n)$ satisfy Assumption~\ref{ass:initial} below, and let the weight $f$ satisfy Assumption~\ref{ass:forcing} above. Then, for almost every $\gamma \in {\mathbb{R}}$, there exists a solution to~\eqref{def:mcf_forcing} with initial hypersurface $\Gamma_0^\gamma :=  \{x \in {\mathbb{R}}^n\colon u^0(x) = \gamma\}$, in the sense that it is both a distributional and a Brakke solution.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{EH}
\[
\frac{d}{dt} v - \Delta_\Gamma v
= -|A|^2 v -\frac{2|\nabla_\Gamma v|^2}{v} - v^2 (\nabla _\Gamma G)\cdot \mathbf{e}_{n+1}.
\]
Note that $v^2$ of the R.H.S. comes from $\frac{d}{dt}v = \frac{d}{dt} \nu_{n+1} ^{-1}= v^2 \frac{d}{dt} \nu_{n+1}$, where $\nu_{n+1} = \frac{1}{v}$ was used.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Set $H=\frac{1}{n} \nabla\cdot \, \left( \frac{\nabla u}{v} \right)$ (see \cite[page 390]{gilbarg_trudinger}). Then, it holds  (see \cite[page 402, eq.~(16.46)]{gilbarg_trudinger}) that
\[
\int_\Gamma (|A|^2 \frac{1}{v} +\Delta_\Gamma \frac{1}{v} + n \delta_{n+1} H) \varphi \, d\mathcal{H}^{n}=0
\]
for any test function $\varphi$.
We compute
\[
\Delta _\Gamma \frac{1}{v}
=\mathrm{div} _\Gamma (- v^{-2} \nabla_\Gamma v)
=2v^{-3} |\nabla_\Gamma v|^2 - v^{-2} \Delta_\Gamma v
\]
and
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
&n \delta_{n+1} H
=\delta_{n+1} \big(\nabla\cdot \big(\frac{\nabla u}{v}\big)\big)
=\delta_{n+1} \left(\frac{\partial_t u}{v} +G\right)\\
=&\, 0 - \left( \big(\nabla \big(\frac{\partial_t u}{v}\big),0\big) \cdot \frac{(-\nabla u,1)}{v}\right) \frac{1}{v}+\delta_{n+1} G \\
=&\, \frac{1}{v^2} \frac{d}{dt} v + \nabla_\Gamma G \cdot \mathrm{e}_{n+1},
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where we used \eqref{v} and $\partial _t v= \frac{\nabla u\cdot \nabla \partial_t u}{v}$. Hence we obtain the claim.

\item $G=\Phi (u)$ with $\Phi'(s) \leq 0$ for any $s\in \mathbb{R}$,

\]

label: cor:max_grad
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:max_grad}
Assume $G=  rac{(-
abla u,1)} {\sqrt{1+|
abla u|^2}} \cdot (
abla f,0)$ for some $f(x,t)$ and there exists $\lambda>0$ such that $\xi^T 
abla ^2 (f(x,t)- rac{\lambda}{2} |x|^2) \xi \leq 0 $ for any $x,\xi\in \mathbb{R}^{n}, t\geq 0$. Then, it holds that
\[
\sqrt{1+|
abla u (x,t)|^2} \leq e^{\lambda t}\sup_x \sqrt{1+|
abla u (x,0)|^2}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Set $\tilde f(x,t):=f(x,t)-\frac{\lambda}{2} |x|^2$.
Following the same procedure as in \eqref{I}, 
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
I=& \, - \nabla u \cdot \nabla \left( \frac{(-\nabla u,1)} {\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}} \cdot (\nabla f,0) \right)
 \\
 =& \, - \nabla u \cdot \nabla \left( \frac{(-\nabla u,1)} {\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}} \cdot (\nabla \tilde f,0) \right)
 - \frac{\lambda}{2}  \nabla u \cdot \nabla \left( \frac{(-\nabla u,1)} {\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}} \cdot (\nabla |x|^2,0) \right)
 \\
\leq &\, 
\mathbf{a} \cdot \nabla_\Gamma (\frac{v^2}{2}) + \frac{\lambda}{2} \frac{1}{v} u_{x_i} u_{x_j} \partial_{x_ix_j} |x|^2
=\mathbf{a} \cdot \nabla_\Gamma (\frac{v^2}{2}) + \lambda \frac{|\nabla u|^2}{v}\\
\leq &\, 
\mathbf{a} \cdot \nabla_\Gamma (\frac{v^2}{2}) + \lambda v
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
holds for some $\mathbf{a}$. Hence, we obtain
\[
\frac{d}{dt} v - \Delta_\Gamma v - v\mathbf{a} \cdot \nabla_\Gamma v \leq \lambda v.
\]
Applying the maximum principle to this inequality for the function $w:=v e^{-\lambda t}$ yields the above assertion.

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $A \subset \{|\nabla u| = 0\} \subset {\mathbb{R}}^n \times [0,\infty)$ be a bounded, measurable subset. We use~\eqref{eq:conv_w}, the local, strong $L^2$ convergence of $e^{f_\varepsilon}$ given by~\eqref{conv:e^f}, the $L^2$ bound of the first variation~\eqref{eq:L2bound_first_variation}, and the weak-$*$ $L^\infty$ convergence of $e^{f_\varepsilon} |\nabla u_\varepsilon|$ by~\eqref{eq:conv_eF_nabla_u} to compute that
        \begin{align*}
            \bigg| \int_{A}  &\partial_t u \ e^{f}  \, dx \,dt \bigg|\\ 
            & =\lim_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0}  \left|  \int_{A} \delta E_\varepsilon(u_\varepsilon) e^{f_\varepsilon} \sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |\nabla u_\varepsilon|^2}  \, dx \, dt \right|\\
            &\leq  \limsup_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0} \left(\int_A |\delta E_\varepsilon(u_\varepsilon)|^2 e^{f_\varepsilon} \sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |\nabla u_\varepsilon|^2} \, dx \, dt\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \left(\int_A e^{f_\varepsilon} \sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |\nabla u_\varepsilon|^2} \, dx \, dt \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
            &\leq C \limsup_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0} \left( \|e^{f_\varepsilon}\|_{L^\infty(A)} |A| \varepsilon + \int_A e^{f_\varepsilon} |\nabla u_\varepsilon| \, dx \,dt \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
            &= 0. 
        \end{align*}
        This concludes the proof as $e^{f}>0$ and $A$ was arbitrary subset of $\{|\nabla u| = 0\}$.

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{the:brakke_u}
    For all $0 \leq t_1 < t_2  < \infty$ and any $\phi \in C_c^\infty({\mathbb{R}}^n 	imes [0, \infty)), \phi \geq 0$ it holds 
     egin{align}
        \int_{{\mathbb{R}}^n} \phi e^f |
abla u| \, dx \Big|_{t = t_2} + \int_{t_1}^{t_2} \int_{{\mathbb{R}}^n} \left(\phi |\delta E(u)|^2  - 
abla \phi \cdot 
u \delta E(u)  - \phi \partial_t f - \partial_t \phi ight) e^f |
abla u|\, dx \, dt 
onumber\
        \leq \int_{{\mathbb{R}}^n} \phi e^f |
abla u| \, dx \Big|_{t = t_1   } \label{eq:edi}.
    \end{align}
    where the integrands are interpreted as being zero on $\{|
abla u| = 0 \}$.

label: eq:approx_edi
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $0 \leq \phi \in C_c^\infty({\mathbb{R}}^n 	imes [0, \infty))$. Recall that $\partial_t u_\varepsilon = -\delta E_\varepsilon(u_\varepsilon) \sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2}$ and $
abla u_\varepsilon \cdot \mathbf{n} = 0$ on $\partial \Omega_\varepsilon$. Hence, we can compute with the help of once integrating by parts that 
         egin{align*}
            rac{d}{dt} \int_{\Omega_\varepsilon }& \phi e^{f_\varepsilon} \sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2}  \, dx \
            =& \int_{\Omega_\varepsilon} \phi  rac{
abla u_\varepsilon \cdot 
abla \partial_t u_\varepsilon}{\sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2}} e^{f_\varepsilon}  + \phi  \partial_t f_\varepsilon e^{f_\varepsilon}\sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2}  + \partial_t \phi  e^{f_\varepsilon}\sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2}\,dx  \
            =& -\int_{\Omega_\varepsilon} \phi |\delta E_{\varepsilon}(u_\varepsilon)|^2 e^{f_\varepsilon}\sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2} -   rac{
abla u_\varepsilon \cdot 
abla \phi}{\sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2}} \delta E_\varepsilon(u_\varepsilon)  e^{f_\varepsilon} \sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2} \
            & + \int_{\Omega_\varepsilon} \phi \partial_t f_\varepsilon e^{f_\varepsilon}  \sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2}+ \partial_t \phi\  e^{f_\varepsilon} \sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2} \, dx.
        \end{align*}
        We post-process this by integrating in time from $0<t_1$ to $t_2 < \infty$ to obtain
         egin{align}
             &\int_{\Omega_\varepsilon} \phi  e^{f_\varepsilon}\sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2} \, dx \Big|_{t = t_2} && - \int_{t_1}^{t_2} \int_{{\mathbb{R}}^n} \phi  \partial_t f_\varepsilon e^{f_\varepsilon}\sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2} + \partial_t \phi  e^{f_\varepsilon}\sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2}\, dx \, dt
onumber\
            & &&+ \int_{t_1}^{t_2}  \int_{\Omega_\varepsilon} \phi |\delta E_{\varepsilon}(u_\varepsilon)|^2 e^{f_\varepsilon}\sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2} \, dx \, dt 
onumber\
             & &&- \int_{t_1}^{t_2}  \int_{\Omega_\varepsilon} 
u_\varepsilon \cdot 
abla \phi\ \delta E_\varepsilon(u_\varepsilon)  e^{f_\varepsilon} \sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2} \, dx\, dt 
onumber\
             &\leq \int_{\Omega_\varepsilon} \phi  e^{f_\varepsilon} \sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2}\, dx&& \hspace{-15pt} \Big|_{t = t_1} \label{eq:approx_edi}.
        \end{align}
        By~\eqref{eq:conv_eF_nabla_u_t} we have for any $s \geq 0$ that
         egin{equation}\label{eq:conv_energy}
            \int_{\Omega_\varepsilon } \phi e^{f_\varepsilon}\sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2}  \, dx\Big|_{t=s} ightarrow \int_{{\mathbb{R}}^n } \phi e^f |
abla u| \, dx \Big|_{t=s}\quad \quad 	ext{ as } \varepsilon \downarrow 0.
        \end{equation}
        We wish to pass to the limit in every term of the approximated energy dissipation inequality~\eqref{eq:approx_edi}. 
        Because $e^{f_\varepsilon }\partial_t f_\varepsilon ightarrow e^f \partial_t f$ and $e^{f_\varepsilon} ightarrow e^f$ strongly in $L^1_{loc}({\mathbb{R}}^n 	imes (0, \infty))$ (as $e^{f_\varepsilon }$ and $\partial_t f_\varepsilon$ both converge in $L^2_{loc}$), we can also pass to the limit in the second term. This yields 
         egin{align}
            \int_{t_1}^{t_2} \int_{\Omega_\varepsilon} \phi \sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2} \partial_t f_\varepsilon e^{f_\varepsilon} + \partial_t \phi \sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2} e^{f_\varepsilon} \, dx \, dt 
onumber\
            ightarrow \int_{t_1}^{t_2} \int_{{\mathbb{R}}^n} (\phi \partial_t f +\partial_t \phi ) e^f |
abla u| \, dx \, dt \quad \quad 	ext{ as } \varepsilon \downarrow 0.\label{eq:second_term}
        \end{align}
        For the third term we will prove the lower-semicontinuity in the form 
         egin{equation}
            \int_{t_1}^{t_2}  \int_{{\mathbb{R}}^n} \phi |\delta E(u)|^2 e^f |
abla u|\, dx \, dt \leq \liminf_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0} \int_{t_1}^{t_2}  \int_{\Omega_\varepsilon}  \phi |\delta E_{\varepsilon}(u_\varepsilon)|^2 e^{f_\varepsilon} \sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2} \, dx \, dt.\label{eq:lsc_first_variation}
        \end{equation}
        To that aim introduce the test function $ho_m(\delta E(u)) \in L^\infty({\mathbb{R}}^n 	imes (0, \infty))$ with
         egin{equation*}
            ho_m(z) = egin{cases}
                 m & 	ext{if } z \geq m,\
                z &	ext{if } -m \leq z \leq m,\
                - m & 	ext{if } z \leq - m.
            \end{cases}
        \end{equation*}
        Recall, that $\delta E_\varepsilon (u_\varepsilon) \sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2} ightharpoonup \delta E(u) |
abla u|$ weakly in $L^2_{loc}({\mathbb{R}}^n 	imes (0,\infty))$ as we have already seen in~\eqref{eq:conv_time}. This yields
         egin{align*}
            \int_{t_1}^{t_2}& \int_{{\mathbb{R}}^n}\phi  ho_m(\delta E(u)) \delta E(u) e^f |
abla u| \, dx \,dt\ &= \lim_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0} \int_{t_1}^{t_2} \int_{\Omega_\varepsilon} \phi  ho_m(\delta E(u))\delta E_\varepsilon(u_\varepsilon)e^{f_\varepsilon} \sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2} \,dx \, dt \
            &\leq \liminf_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0} \left(\int_{t_1}^{t_2} \int_{\Omega_\varepsilon} \phi |\delta E_\varepsilon(u_\varepsilon)|^2 e^{f_\varepsilon}\sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2} \,dx \,dt ight)^{ rac{1}{2}}\
            &\hspace{200pt}	imes\left(\int_{t_1}^{t_2} \int_{{\mathbb{R}}^n} \phi ho_m(\delta E(u))^2 e^f |
abla u| \, dx \,dt ight)^{ rac{1}{2}} \
            &\leq \liminf_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0} \left(\int_{t_1}^{t_2} \int_{\Omega_\varepsilon} \phi |\delta E_\varepsilon(u_\varepsilon)|^2  e^{f_\varepsilon}\sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2} \,dx \,dt ight)^{ rac{1}{2}} \
            &\hspace{200pt}	imes\left(\int_{t_1}^{t_2} \int_{{\mathbb{R}}^n} \phi ho_m(\delta E(u)) \delta E(u)e^f|
abla u| \, dx \,dt ight)^{ rac{1}{2}},
        \end{align*}
        where we used $ho_m(\delta E(u))^2 \leq ho_m(\delta E(u)) \delta E(u)$ in the last estimate. The monotone convergence theorem lets us pass to the limit $m ightarrow \infty$ to conclude the desired inequality~\eqref{eq:lsc_first_variation}.

        In the last term we utilize the strong $L^2_{loc}$-convergence \eqref{eqref:strong_normals} of the normals and~\eqref{conv:e^f} of $e^{f_\varepsilon}$ and once more the weak convergence of $\delta E_\varepsilon (u_\varepsilon) \sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2} $ to compute
         egin{multline*}
            \lim_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0} \int_{t_1}^{t_2}  \int_{\Omega_\varepsilon\cap \{|
abla u| > 0 \}} 
u_\varepsilon \cdot 
abla \phi\ \delta E_\varepsilon(u_\varepsilon)  e^{f_\varepsilon} \sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2} \, dx\, dt \
            =\int_{t_1}^{t_2}  \int_{{\mathbb{R}}^n \cap \{|
abla u| > 0 \}} 
u \cdot 
abla \phi\ \delta E(u)  e^f |
abla u| \, dx\, dt.
        \end{multline*}
        Note we have already witnessed in~\eqref{eq:vanish_remainder} that the integral over the remaining integration domain vanishes. Hence, it holds 
         egin{equation}\label{eq:fourth_term}
                \int_{t_1}^{t_2}  \int_{\Omega_\varepsilon } 
u_\varepsilon \cdot 
abla \phi\ \delta E_\varepsilon(u_\varepsilon)  e^{f_\varepsilon} \sqrt{\varepsilon^2 + |
abla u_\varepsilon|^2} \, dx\, dt ightarrow   \int_{t_1}^{t_2}  \int_{{\mathbb{R}}^n} 
u \cdot 
abla \phi\ \delta E(u)  e^f |
abla u| \, dx\, dt
        \end{equation}
        where we once again identify the right-hand side integrand as zero on $\{|
abla u| = 0\}$.

        The final inequality~\eqref{eq:edi} follows by passing to the limit in~\eqref{eq:approx_edi} with the help of~\eqref{eq:conv_energy}, \eqref{eq:second_term}, \eqref{eq:lsc_first_variation} and~\eqref{eq:fourth_term}.
